Union prevailing wage totals $56.12 an hour: $33.86 in base wage, $7.10 in health insurance and $15.16 in retirement and other benefits. Nonunion market-rate totals $40.27 an hour: $28.95 in base wage and $11.32 in combined benefits.

alt://d3k81ch9hvuctc.cloudfront.net/company/U6eiKq/images/42950ddd-d698-4950-9cfd-54ff0c585bb2.png|Day one: where the construction money comes from. The affordable project assembles $105 million from seven sources including $44 million in federal and state tax credit equity, $29 million in state and city subsidy, $13 million in affordable condo sales, $10 million in library funds and $8 million in bank debt. The market-rate project assembles $70 million from just two: $45 million in bank debt and $25 million in investor equity demanding 15 to 20 percent returns.

alt://d3k81ch9hvuctc.cloudfront.net/company/U6eiKq/images/7d1fcc1e-9375-4ef1-9929-899c9e008cc5.png|Thirty years of carbon: the same 110 homes, built two ways. A code-built, gas-heated building emits about 10,650 cumulative tons of CO2e over thirty years, while a Passive House, all-electric building emits about 2,310 tons. The roughly 8,300 tons avoided is like removing about 1,800 cars from the road for a year.

alt://d3k81ch9hvuctc.cloudfront.net/company/U6eiKq/images/f342ffd5-916f-4bcb-9886-ad480162bc15.png|Year 30: where thirty years of money ended up. The affordable building cycles $72 million total through operating costs, debt service, reserves and resident services, plus a capped nonprofit developer total. The market-rate building generates $390 million, including $148 million in owner operating income and $151 million in building value owned free of restrictions at year 30.

alt://d3k81ch9hvuctc.cloudfront.net/company/U6eiKq/images/f82612b3-7d64-4bc1-9563-be9c7332aba7.png|One 2-bedroom apartment over thirty years. The affordable unit totals $1.11 million, with the family paying about $1.1 million in rent and the nonprofit developer share capped at $230,000. The market-rate unit totals $3.73 million, with the family paying about $2.3 million in rent, $1.41 million going to owner operating income and $1.45 million to the owner's share of the building at year 30.
